title: Normalized presentations and actual coefficient-comparison data for tensor exchange
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data and the four finite-Tor categories of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], a separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ of finite-type schemes over the fixed algebraic closure, a compactification $c$, and a constructible exceptional-adjunction System. Use the tensor--Hom models and their ringed/partial realizations of [def-sf-tensor-hom-transposition-data]. A Presentation consists of a Model at every stage, its RingModel and normalized Projection at every ring stage, and its integral, rational and common-stage partial realizations on X and Y. It contains no exchange isomorphism, shift structure on Hom, or coefficient-transposition conclusion. NormalizedDatum means that these ingredients realize the given six-functor datum: at every finite field it retains normalized higher operations, at the original field they equal the supplied higher operations; ordinary and exceptional Hom transposes are preserved at the finite, integral, rational and common stages; rational/common projections are precisely the datum's actual projection, conjugated by the recorded tensor comparisons and signed braidings.

A Change compares two such models by exceptional, tensor, pullback and projection comparison isomorphisms. Its Hom maps are the transposes of the extended evaluations; its ordinary-direct-image map is the counit mate of pullback. Compatible is equality of the two inverse-exchange routes. ChangeShifts is naturality and both signed first/unsigned second Hom shift equations for these same component maps, together with the direct-image shift equation. CoefficientComparisons retains the four actual System coefficient witnesses (allowed ring changes, rationalization, rational scalar extension and common inclusion); its shift evidence is attached to each of these witnesses, rather than quantified over arbitrary Changes. CorePackage adds exchange Conclusions, finite RingShifts, Compatible for all Changes and those CoefficientComparisons to a Presentation. Package adds NormalizedDatum's precise realizations to such a CorePackage. The compactification square and the tensor-coordinate conversions in these formulas are the identity square at $f,c$ and the published normalization equalities. These are data and predicates, not existence assertions.
